pr_title: fix(core): handle pluralize functions that expect a number
pr_body:
Previously we were passing a string form of the value to pluralize
to the `getLocalePluralCase()` function that is extracted from the
locale data. But some locales have functions that rely upon this
value being a number not a string.

Now we convert the value to a number before passing it to the
locale data function.

Fixes #36888

issue_context.title: [i18n] Different ICU and NgPlural behaviour when using sourceLocale
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Description I found out that using a custom `sourceLocale` configuration ("es" in my case), the result from this code is unexpected: ```
{{ case }} ICU: {case, plural, zero {zero} one {one} other {other}} NgPlural: zero one other
``` ### Expected: 0 ICU: other NgPlural: other 1 ICU: one NgPlural: one 2 ICU: other NgPlural: other ### Received: 0 ICU: other NgPlural: other 1 ICU: **other** NgPlural: one 2 ICU: other NgPlural: other ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction I haven't been able to reproduce it in Stackblitz, it doesn't recognize `sourceLocale` configuration in `angular.json` https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-g47pyh Using CLI: ng new project Enable `localize` and set `sourceLocale` to "es" in angular.json Copy the above code and run the project ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

@angular-devkit/architect         0.901.4
@angular-devkit/build-angular     0.901.4
@angular-devkit/build-optimizer   0.901.4
@angular-devkit/build-webpack     0.901.4
@angular-devkit/core              9.1.4
@angular-devkit/schematics        9.1.4
@ngtools/webpack                  9.1.4
@schematics/angular               9.1.4
@schematics/update                0.901.4
rxjs                              6.5.5
typescript                        3.8.3
webpack                           4.42.0
**Anything else relevant?** I'm using Windows
comments:
Here's the problem:

![Screenshot 2020-05-02 at 21 22 34](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15655/80891332-35f14a00-8cbb-11ea-9cf8-c93dec2aea95.png)

It appears that Ivy passes a string form of the number through to the pluralization function, whereas ngPlural passes through the number form.

We actually strip out the conversion from string to number in the generated plural CLDR functions: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/12fcc7cafe8bf6dd33416847327891b581281774/tools/gulp-tasks/cldr/extract.js#L571

This is to keep the size of the locale data files to a minimum, I believe.

So I think the best fix is to ensure that we only pass a number to these generated functions, by fixing it here: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/12fcc7cafe8bf6dd33416847327891b581281774/packages/core/src/i18n/localization.ts#L15

Originally I did do that. But the resulting expectations are different so it just becomes a confusion of conditionals.

I'll update the test descriptions.

It looks like we need to update `value` argument type, since we handle other types below as well (i.e. `typeof value === 'string' ? parseInt(value, 10) : value`). I'd also propose adding an inline comment on why we do that (as it's explained in PR description).
As it turns out this is always a string... So perhaps we should just avoid the `typeof value === 'string'` check?
